channel.title: Skeptics Society-Skeptic Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Skeptics Society-Skeptic Magazine (skeptic.com)

item.title: From Sisterhood to Mean Girls: Evolutionary Insights Into Friendship and Fiendship
item.description: Friendship can be a source of strength—or betrayal. This article explores the hidden evolutionary forces behind women’s closest bonds, the rise of the “frenemy,” and how covert competition, gossip, and loyalty shape relationships across a lifetime.

item.title: The Other Lab Leak Hypothesis: Is Lyme Disease Caused by an Escaped Bioweapon?
item.description: Is Lyme disease a weaponized pathogen from a secret lab? While rumors point to Plum Island, scientific evidence shows the bacteria existed in museum specimens long before the facility opened.

item.title: The Case for Free Speech Maximalism
item.description: Dismissed as a naïve pitstop for testosterone-soaked young men, free speech maximalism gets a feisty, personal defense from a 69-year-old woman who argues that you are not safer for knowing less about what people really think—and that restricting offense will ultimately silence us all.

item.title: Confessions of a Former Chiropractor
item.description: Chiropractor-turned-statistician J. Michael Menke exposes the profession from the inside: the pseudoscience, the sales culture, the millionaire coaches, and why “helping 50 percent of patients” is nothing to celebrate.

item.title: Robert Trivers (1943–2026) Reflects on His Life and Work
item.description: Robert Trivers looks back on his life and tells the story of how he became an evolutionary biologist, reflecting on science, mental illness, mentors, ambition, and self-deception. Through encounters with major thinkers, he offers a candid look at human nature, conflict, and the search for truth.

item.title: The Rise of Decorative Neuroscience
item.description: Are neuroscience buzzwords making us smarter, or just easier to manipulate? Tommy Blanchard exposes how brain-science jargon dresses up tired advice, why it works on us, and what we should be asking instead.

item.title: Robert L. Trivers, Evolutionary Biologist Who Transformed the Science of Social Behavior, Dies at 83
item.description: Robert Ludlow “Bob” Trivers, one of the most consequential evolutionary biologists of the twentieth century, died on March 12, 2026, at the age of 83. item.description: Robert Trivers, who died on March 12, 2026, was arguably the most important evolutionary theorist since Darwin. item.title: Selling Fear and Half-Truths: The Latest 60 Minutes ‘Exposé’ on Havana Syndrome
item.description: 60 Minutes has aired four Havana Syndrome exposés—but two intelligence assessments say attacks are “highly unlikely.” Robert Bartholomew, a scholar of mass delusion, reveals the omissions, conflicts of interest, and psychology of belief driving one of TV journalism’s most credulous narratives.
